text:
incidents-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: High tail latency and streaming stalls detected in inference path. Automated pager triggered for p99 spike (>3s). Affected subsystems: control-plane config-fetch, auth token DB, streaming tail queues. Paging on-call. :rotating_light:

ben-sre: I'm on it, looking at the control-plane metrics now. p95 jumped ~2.5x, p99 is around 3.2s for inference responses, streaming stalls visible on tail consumers.

alex-plat: Noted. Saw error rate for streaming sessions up ~1.1% and a lot of 504s from /config/fetch. Linking dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/inf-path/p99-spike

tara-backend: Repro-ing a quick curl to configfetch shows timeouts. ```curl -v https://control-plane.internal/config/fetch -H 'x-customer: cust-123'``` yields `504` after 10s.

ben-sre: Querying DB connections to token-store, looks saturated. `SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state = 'active';` shows many long-running queries for auth lookups.

devon-security: Any recent changes to feature flags or rate-limits? I saw a rollout of a new feature-flag evaluation path earlier today that calls configfetch more frequently.

alex-plat: Yes, feature flag rollout `ff/fast-eval` started at 07:12 UTC. Canary was 5% but seen traffic spike when client SDK hammered control-plane with repeated fetches.

ben-sre: Ok, immediate mitigation plan: 1) pause feature-flag rollout 2) enable cached-config fallback for SDKs 3) temporarily increase DB connection pool for token-store 4) add short-term rate-limit override for internal CIP (control-plane) from platform tier. I'll execute 1 and 2 now.

oncall-bot: Handoff: ben-sre is on-call owner for this incident. Escalation to SRE lead if not resolved in 30m.

ben-sre: Paused rollout: `kubectl -n control-plane set env deployment/ff-evaluator PAUSE_ROLLOUT=true` ✅

ben-sre: Enabled cached-config fallback via config: `rcp set controlplane.cache_hard_fallback=true` ✅ — clients should start hitting cached configs within ~15s.

tara-backend: Pushed a hotfix to reduce calls: added jitter + backoff in SDK for 1 minute to reduce thundering herd. Patch ID `hotfix/2071234567-ff-backoff` — rolling.

alex-plat: DB pool bump: increased token-store max_connections from 120 -> 250 for the replica set. Applied to staging and prod proxies. Watch for queueing.

devon-security: Monitoring auth latencies now. Any abnormal auth errors?

ben-sre: Error rates dropped after cache fallback but p99 still elevated due to some long-running streaming tails in the inference runtime. Investigating whether streaming stalls are downstream of config fetchs or independent.

tara-backend: Found a subset of requests that still call feature-eval sync path and block streaming IO. Grep logs: `grep "fast-eval" /var/log/control-plane/* | wc -l` shows ~7k calls in 5m - most from one SDK version.

alex-plat: We should block that SDK version at the edge for now. I can add a rule to the ingress LB to return cached config for that user-agent.

ben-sre: Applying temporary ingress rule to return 200 cached payload for UA `redwood-sdk/1.3.2` — applied.

oncall-bot: Customer impact note: 3 enterprise customers with long-tail streaming sessions experienced intermittent stalls (manual reports coming in). Severity: S2.

devon-security: Any risk with the DB pool bump? Watch for memory/cpu on replicas.

ben-sre: Watching. CPU spiked briefly on replica-1 but stabilized. No OOMs.

tara-backend: After ingress rule + cache fallback, streaming stall count dropped ~70% in the last 5m. p95 ~420ms, p99 ~1.1s now (improvement).

alex-plat: Rolling metrics posted: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/inf-path/response-latency?from=now-30m

ben-sre: Still seeing a small tail cluster at ~1.2-1.5s from requests that hit auth DB for legacy tokens. Plan: deploy a short-lived read-replica to offload heavy auth reads, and add a query timeout to token lookup (200ms) to fail fast and fallback to cached token map.

tara-backend: Deploying read-replica now (task `deploy/replica-auth-207123`). ETA ~8m.

devon-security: We should notify Customer Success for the 3 affected tenants. I'm drafting an interim message that we experienced control-plane load causing intermittent streaming stalls; mitigation in progress; no data exfiltration.

ben-sre: Read-replica up and syncing. Added token lookup timeout in code path and enabled graceful fallback to cached map. Rolling this change to control-plane pods.

ben-sre: Both mitigations are in; I see auth read latency tail collapse. p99 now at ~480ms.

oncall-bot: Update: paging timer reset. If p99 stays <600ms for next 20m, we'll de-escalate.

alex-plat: Customer Success notified for the three enterprises with short message and link to status page.

tara-backend: Postmortem owners? I nominate @alex-plat for root cause (feature-flag rollout + SDK thundering herd) and @ben-sre for mitigation timeline.

devon-security: Assigning postmortem: `incidents/2071234567-retry-storm-rca` in the triage board. Please include: traffic patterns, SDK versions, rollout config, and mitigation steps.

ben-sre: Final notes: root cause appears to be a canary rollout that exposed an inefficient sync feature-eval path in SDK that multiplied configfetch calls, overwhelming auth/token DB and causing control-plane timeouts. Mitigations applied: pause rollout, cached-fallback, ingress UA rule, DB pool bump, read-replica, query timeouts.

alex-plat: Recommend follow-ups: set stricter rate-limits for control-plane per-client, require SDK to use async eval by default, add rollout ramp protections (circuit-breaker) if backend error rates cross threshold.

oncall-bot: Incident marked: mitigation successful. Monitoring for 30m. Postmortem owner(s) assigned. :white_check_mark:

ben-sre: I'll leave the thread open for 30m then close. Thanks all, great quick ops.

tara-backend: Thx — will open PR for the SDK changes and add e2e to catch thundering-fallthrough.

devon-security: Closing customer comms after final monitoring window.

ben-sre: Closing thread in 21m unless regressions.
